note: One functional task per skill. Assertions check objectively-verifiable C64 facts the skill should get right (and baseline Claude often gets wrong). Graded on the final answer text/code the run produces.

evals.prompt: I'm brand new to Commodore 64 programming. Give me a short orientation: the main chips, roughly where they live in the memory map, and where I'd look for sound vs sprites vs reading a joystick vs the disk drive.
assertions: Names the VIC-II at $D000 (53248)
Names the SID at $D400 (54272)
Names the two CIA chips at $DC00 and $DD00
States KERNAL ROM at $E000 and BASIC ROM at $A000
Points sound to SID, sprites to VIC/sprites, joystick to control ports/CIA, disk to the disk topic

evals.prompt: Write a Commodore 64 BASIC program that asks the user for their name with INPUT and then prints HELLO followed by the name five times using a FOR/NEXT loop.
assertions: Uses INPUT with a string variable (name ending in $)
Uses a FOR ... NEXT loop iterating 5 times
Uses numbered BASIC lines
Concatenates/prints HELLO together with the name variable
Is valid runnable C64 BASIC V2 (no non-existent keywords)

evals.prompt: In C64 BASIC, how do I clear the screen and print the word READY in white? Give the exact CHR$ codes, and explain why the screen code I'd POKE to screen memory for the letter A is different from its PETSCII/CHR$ code.
assertions: Gives CHR$(147) to clear the screen
Gives CHR$(5) for white text
States screen code for A is 1 while PETSCII/CHR$ for A is 65
Explains POKEing screen RAM uses screen codes, PRINT/CHR$ uses PETSCII

evals.prompt: Explain what each of these C64 keys/combos does: the Commodore (C=) key, RUN/STOP, RESTORE, RUN/STOP+RESTORE together, and the function keys f1 through f8.
assertions: C= key: with SHIFT switches upper-case/graphics vs upper/lower charset (and/or color selection)
RUN/STOP + RESTORE performs a warm reset / returns to BASIC (RESTORE triggers an NMI)
Explains only f1/f3/f5/f7 are unshifted and f2/f4/f6/f8 need SHIFT
Does not invent non-existent behavior

evals.prompt: Show me how to switch the C64 into standard high-resolution bitmap mode from BASIC, with the bitmap at $2000 and screen memory at $0400. Which registers/POKEs set this up?
assertions: Sets the bitmap mode bit (BMM, bit 5) in $D011 / location 53265
Sets $D018 / location 53272 so the bitmap base points at $2000
Mentions the bitmap is 8000 bytes
Mentions color comes from screen RAM (and clearing the bitmap)

evals.prompt: Give me a Commodore 64 BASIC program that enables sprite 0, sets its data pointer, positions it at X=160 Y=100, and colors it red.
assertions: POKEs 53269 ($D015) to enable sprite 0 (value 1)
Sets the sprite 0 pointer at 2040 (end of screen RAM)
POKEs 53287 ($D027) to 2 for red

evals.prompt: Explain how to set up a raster interrupt on the C64 that fires at raster line 100, in 6510 assembly: which registers to set, the 9th raster bit, enabling the interrupt, and acknowledging it.
assertions: Writes 100 to $D012 and handles the 9th bit (bit 7 of $D011, cleared for line 100)
Enables the raster interrupt by setting bit 0 of $D01A
Acknowledges the interrupt by writing to $D019 in the handler
Sets the IRQ vector ($0314/$0315 or $FFFE) and uses SEI/CLI appropriately

evals.prompt: Write code (BASIC or 6510 assembly) to play roughly a one-second note on voice 1 of the SID using a sawtooth waveform, with a simple envelope.
assertions: Sets master volume in $D418 / 54296 (low nibble, e.g. 15)
Sets voice 1 frequency in $D400/$D401
Sets the voice 1 control register $D404 to a sawtooth+gate value (sawtooth bit 32 + gate 1 = 33)
Sets attack/decay $D405 and sustain/release $D406
Clears the gate bit afterwards to release the note

evals.prompt: Write a 6510 machine-language routine, callable from BASIC with SYS 49152, that fills the C64 text screen with character code 81 (the ball). Show the assembly and how to enter and call it.
assertions: Places the routine at $C000 (49152)
Loads #81 into A and stores across the 1000 bytes of screen RAM at $0400-$07E7
Ends the routine with RTS to return to BASIC
Shows calling it with SYS 49152
The screen-fill loop is correct (covers all 1000 cells, e.g. 4 pages via an index loop)

evals.prompt: Using KERNAL routines from 6510 assembly, print the two-character string HI to the screen. Give the routine address(es) and which register holds what.
assertions: Uses CHROUT at $FFD2
Puts the character to print in the accumulator A
Uses PETSCII codes 72 for H and 73 for I
Calls CHROUT once per character (or loops)

evals.prompt: I want to copy the C64 character ROM into RAM at $3000 so I can edit the font. Explain the banking I need to do with $01 to see the character ROM, and why interrupts matter.
assertions: Explains the character ROM appears at $D000-$DFFF when CHAREN (bit 2 of $01) is cleared
Sets $01 to $33 (or otherwise clears bit 2) to expose char ROM, then restores it (e.g. $37)
Disables interrupts (SEI) during the copy because the I/O area is banked out
Copies 4096 bytes (2 char sets) or 2048 per set to $3000

evals.prompt: Write 6510 code to set CIA #1 Timer A to generate an IRQ about 60 times per second, and explain the registers involved.
assertions: Loads the Timer A latch at $DC04/$DC05
Enables the Timer A interrupt in the ICR $DC0D (with bit 7 set to mark 'set', bit 0 for timer A)
Starts the timer via control register A $DC0E (with continuous reload)
Acknowledges/handles by reading $DC0D in the IRQ handler

evals.prompt: In C64 BASIC, how do I open a channel to the printer (device 4), send one line of text to it, and close the channel?
assertions: Uses OPEN with device number 4 (e.g. OPEN 4,4)
Uses PRINT# to the opened file number to send the text
Uses CLOSE on the file number
Device/secondary-address usage is correct for a printer

evals.prompt: Give me the C64 BASIC commands to: (1) list the directory of a 1541 disk, (2) load a program called GAME, (3) format a new disk, and (4) read the disk drive's error channel.
assertions: Directory: LOAD"$",8 then LIST
Load: LOAD"GAME",8
Format: OPEN 15,8,15 then PRINT#15,"N0:label,id" (NEW)
Error channel: read via the command channel 15 (OPEN 15,8,15 then INPUT#15)

evals.prompt: How do I save a BASIC program to cassette tape on the C64 and load it back later? And if there are several programs on the tape, how do I get to a specific one?
assertions: SAVE"NAME" (device 1 is the default for tape, optionally SAVE"NAME",1)
LOAD"NAME" searches forward for that named program; LOAD with no name loads the next program
Explains tape is sequential with no random-access directory
Mentions practical ways to find a program (tape counter / forward search / header messages)

evals.prompt: Write C64 BASIC to read the joystick in control port 2 and print which direction is being pushed (and whether fire is pressed). Which memory location and bits do I read?
assertions: Reads control port 2 at 56320 ($DC00, CIA1 port A)
Treats the direction bits 0-3 as up/down/left/right
Treats bit 4 as the fire button
Notes the bits are active-LOW (0 = pressed)

evals.prompt: My Commodore 64 powers on (power LED is on) but the screen is completely blank — no border, no text. What are the most likely hardware causes and what should I check first?
assertions: Names the PLA (906114 / 82S100) as a common cause of no-boot/blank screen
Mentions checking the power supply / 5V rail
Mentions RAM and/or the kernal/clock as suspects
Gives a sensible first-check ordering rather than vague advice

evals.prompt: I dumped a .prg and it begins with these bytes: 01 08 0B 08 0A 00 9E 32 30 36 31 00 00 00. Walk me through what this file is and where the actual machine code starts executing.
assertions: Identifies the first two bytes 01 08 as the load address $0801
Identifies a tokenized BASIC line: line number 10, SYS token ($9E)
Decodes the digits 32 30 36 31 as ASCII '2061' — the SYS target
Concludes the machine code starts at $080D (2061) after the BASIC stub
